findings.title: Document every exported ActionList part
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer uses ActionList.Divider between groups or composes ActionList.GroupHeading.TrailingAction to add an action to a group heading, relying on the package documentation to discover its required props and composition location.
findings.observedGap: The parent API exports Divider and nests TrailingAction under GroupHeading, while ActionList.docs.json has no Divider or GroupHeading.TrailingAction entry. Those public parts therefore lack a complete documented owner/required-props/composition contract.
findings.additiveFix: Extend the ActionList documentation metadata and docs examples to include every exported part, including Divider and GroupHeading.TrailingAction, with required props, default element/ref behavior, and supported composition path; do not remove or rename existing exports.

findings.title: Make polymorphism available across the parts surface
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer needs a semantic custom element or router link for a list part such as Item, Group, Divider, Description, or a Visual; current typed APIs either lack as or explicitly state that Item as has no effect.
findings.observedGap: The accepted target requires as on every part, but only selected parts provide useful polymorphism. ActionList.Item’s as is deprecated/no-op, while Group, Divider, Description, and Visuals expose fixed element props.
findings.additiveFix: Add appropriately typed as support to each part while preserving current default markup, behavior, refs, and existing props. Resolve and document target-unspecified part defaults during human rollout; do not assume one element fits every part.

findings.title: Add render forms to ActionList parts
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer needs to render an ActionList part through a supplied element or render function while forwarding its required props, current state, and ref to a custom host.
findings.observedGap: No public part accepts the target element/function render contract; ActionList.Item renderItem is a different legacy callback. ActionList/shared.ts:68-73; ActionList/index.ts:27-61.
findings.additiveFix: Add element and function render forms to the parts while retaining existing part props, callback signatures, and renderItem behavior.

findings.title: Preserve ActionList item handlers and behavior props
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer supplies onClick to an ActionList.Item in a selectable/list context and expects the documented onSelect selection path to continue; a consumer also adds a Group className to customize its appearance.
findings.observedGap: Consumer props spread after menuItemProps can replace the generated onClick handler and behavior attributes, including role, tabIndex, and selection ARIA state.
findings.additiveFix: Keep consumer DOM attributes available while composing consumer handlers and applying ActionList-owned behavior props after the consumer spread.

findings.title: Expose an additive selection transition callback
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer handles pointer or keyboard activation of a selectable ActionList.Item and updates its selected prop based on the selection transition.
findings.observedGap: The only public selection callback is onSelect(event); it does not report the proposed selected value, reason, or synchronous cancel contract required by the target transition callback.
findings.additiveFix: Keep onSelect unchanged and add a separately named object callback carrying the proposed selected value, reason, originating event when present, and synchronous cancel(). Treat the callback name/coexistence shape as a pending maintainer decision.

findings.title: Align the GroupHeading stable selector with its API name
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer or test selects the public ActionList.GroupHeading part using its documented stable data-component identifier.
findings.observedGap: GroupHeading emits data-component="GroupHeadingWrap" rather than the public API name ActionList.GroupHeading; the current selector test asserts the legacy mismatch.
findings.additiveFix: Add data-component="ActionList.GroupHeading" at the public part root and preserve GroupHeadingWrap as a compatibility alias/selector during migration; update tests and docs to identify the public selector.

findings.title: Place ActionList CSS Modules in the component layer
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer applies an unlayered override to ActionList and expects the component’s authored styles to participate in the documented Primer component cascade layer.
findings.observedGap: ActionList.module.css, Group.module.css, and Heading.module.css contain authored CSS rules without @layer primer.components.ActionList.
findings.additiveFix: Wrap each ActionList-owned CSS Module rule set in @layer primer.components.ActionList while retaining the existing class names and declarations.

findings.title: Order ActionList.Group classes component-first
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer needs a semantic custom element or router link for a list part such as Item, Group, Divider, Description, or a Visual; current typed APIs either lack as or explicitly state that Item as has no effect.
findings.observedGap: ActionList.Group combines consumer className before the component class, contrary to ADR-025.
findings.additiveFix: Keep existing Group props and child structure; use component-first class ordering on the configured subcomponent.

findings.title: Documented hook composition spreads the wrong object
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer follows the README and writes the shown Tab/TabList/TabPanel wrappers; each hook result is spread directly, leaving the nested role/ARIA/event props unapplied.
findings.observedGap: The public README tells consumers to spread hook results, but useTab/useTabList/useTabPanel return named nested prop bags. The example fails to realize the documented accessible parts contract.
findings.additiveFix: Correct the example to destructure tabProps, tabListProps, and tabPanelProps (or change the documented API shape additively); add a small docs typecheck/example test. Preserve current hook names and signatures.

findings.title: Public parts lack the uniform substitution and merge contract
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer builds a custom Tab around useTab or uses useTabList/useTabPanel to compose a different semantic element; the hooks provide fixed prop bags and no supported as or render API.
findings.observedGap: The public parts do not support target-required as substitution, and therefore do not define the complete part-level handler/class/style/attribute/ref/behavior ownership rules. Convenience component implementations are not part of the public experimental barrel.
findings.additiveFix: Add a composable part API with as and the agreed render contract while preserving the existing hooks and their prop-getter signatures; define and test target merge order, consumer-first classes, consumer-winning ordinary attrs/styles, final-element refs, and part-owned behavior props.

findings.title: Selection transitions have no additive cancellable callback
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer uses controlled or uncontrolled Tabs and needs the reason/event for a selection transition or needs to synchronously cancel an uncontrolled commit.
findings.observedGap: onValueChange only receives {value}; it cannot report reason/event or cancel the pending internal state update.
findings.additiveFix: Keep onValueChange unchanged and add a separately named transition callback with value, reason, event when present, and synchronous cancel(); decide the new callback name during rollout.

findings.title: Tabs is nested below the required source component directory level
findings.reachableUseCase: A maintainer navigates the component source or tooling expects one PascalCase component directory directly under packages/react/src.
findings.observedGap: Tabs lives at packages/react/src/experimental/Tabs rather than directly at packages/react/src/Tabs; ADR-013's component-directory placement is unmet.
findings.additiveFix: If retaining this experimental API, align its source ownership with the required component directory convention without changing the existing @primer/react/experimental entry point.

findings.title: Public part props omit stable component identity
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer or test needs to select a Tabs tab/panel by a stable component selector independent of its changing selected state.
findings.observedGap: The hooks supply roles, IDs, and data-selected, but no stable data-component identity distinct from state.
findings.additiveFix: Add stable data-component identity to the public part props and document/test it separately from data-selected; preserve the existing ARIA and state attributes.

findings.title: Add a uniform consumer-composable TreeView parts surface
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer using <TreeView><TreeView.Item as={CustomLink}>... needs to compose or replace an interactive tree region while retaining TreeView context, item state, required semantics, and refs; the existing compound API has only an Item-specific as path and no uniform root/part contract.
findings.observedGap: TreeView exposes legacy compound subcomponents, but there is no parts surface giving each interactive part its required props/state/ref and consistent composition contract.
findings.additiveFix: Add a target-aligned parts API alongside the current compound components; define root/item boundaries and document required behavior/state/ref. Keep exact part names/default elements pending maintainer review; preserve existing props, slots, subcomponents, and Item.as behavior.

findings.title: Complete TreeView root DOM and ref conventions
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer needs to focus, measure, scroll, or attach a DOM attribute such as id to the tree container while retaining role=tree and internal keyboard management.
findings.observedGap: TreeViewProps exposes only aria-label/labelledby, children, flat, truncate, className, and style; Root is not ref-forwarding and has only a private ref to its <ul>.
findings.additiveFix: Extend the root API with a forwarded ref and appropriate <ul> DOM props while keeping TreeView-owned role, keyboard handlers, and accessibility attributes authoritative. Add root as only if a reviewed semantic polymorphism use case exists.

findings.title: Add render forms to TreeView parts
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer composing a future TreeView part may need an element or render-function replacement receiving required tree behavior and current item state.
findings.observedGap: TreeView has no part element or function render contract. TreeView.tsx:226-239,250-253.
findings.additiveFix: Add element and function render forms to the parts while retaining existing tree behavior and callbacks.

findings.title: Order TreeView root classes component-first
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer supplies root className while TreeView adds its root reset/module class.
findings.observedGap: TreeView.Root combines consumer className before the component class, contrary to ADR-025.
findings.additiveFix: Keep the current root API and use component-first class ordering in a compatible migration.

findings.title: Add an object-shaped expanded-state transition callback
findings.reachableUseCase: A controlled consumer needs to distinguish pointer, keyboard, and programmatic expansion, inspect the originating event, or synchronously cancel a proposed expansion.
findings.observedGap: The existing onExpandedChange callback receives only a boolean; it lacks the target reason/event/cancel contract.
findings.additiveFix: Add a separately named object callback carrying expanded, reason, event when present, and synchronous cancel(); preserve onExpandedChange(expanded) unchanged. Resolve the additive name during maintainer review.

findings.title: Add a stable public TreeView component selector
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer or integration test needs a stable selector independent of private CSS-module hashes and state attributes.
findings.observedGap: The root has role=tree and implementation data attributes but no stable data-component identity or documented public selector.
findings.additiveFix: Add a stable data-component identifier to the root, document it, and test identity separately from state data attributes.

findings.title: Place TreeView CSS Module rules in its Primer cascade layer
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer styles TreeView alongside Primer utility/component layers and expects the documented component layer ordering.
findings.observedGap: The authored TreeView CSS Module contains unlayered rules rather than @layer primer.components.TreeView.
findings.additiveFix: Wrap the TreeView component rules in @layer primer.components.TreeView without changing selectors or declarations.

findings.title: Add Storybook Playwright interaction coverage for TreeView
findings.reachableUseCase: A keyboard or pointer user expands/collapses an item, moves focus, or loads asynchronous children; these behaviors currently have unit coverage but no Storybook Playwright interaction path.
findings.observedGap: The TreeView Playwright suite visits stories and captures VRT screenshots only; its tests do not interact with the component.
findings.additiveFix: Add a Storybook Playwright test exercising a representative keyboard/pointer tree interaction and asserting focus/expanded behavior; keep unit tests and visual snapshots.

findings.title: Compose TreeView item keyboard handlers
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer using <TreeView><TreeView.Item as={CustomLink}>... needs to compose or replace an interactive tree region while retaining TreeView context, item state, required semantics, and refs; the existing compound API has only an Item-specific as path and no uniform root/part contract.
findings.observedGap: A consumer-supplied onKeyDown is accepted in TreeView.Item props but replaced by the internal handler.
findings.additiveFix: Compose the consumer handler with TreeView keyboard behavior while preserving the existing onSelect and expansion callback signatures.
